rv.q: While no one is a literal captive at a play, there’s something about being stuck for a while in discomfort, in uncertainty, and just having to wait and — as the Greek root of theater reminds us — see.
Blood of the Lamb is a powerful play with a powerful and relevant message for today.
The two actors are strong enough to make for an engrossing hour of theater, but it’s not enough to overcome the areas where Blood of the Lamb falters.
This galvanizing production of intelligent arguments, humorous fumbles, and desperate attempts at humanity is a must see.
As agitprop, Blood of the Lamb holds one’s attention and skillfully depicts a situation that, if it hasn’t yet occurred, seems frighteningly imminent.

cn.t: Hutton's timely abortion-rights drama delivers urgent, powerful impact but suffers from contrivances and lack of texture. Strong performances can't fully overcome the play's structural weaknesses in this 75-minute two-hander.
